# Sirach Chapter 27 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 27 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 27 opens with the dangers of trade (vv. 1-3), then uses a series of sifting/testing metaphors to argue that character is revealed under pressure (vv. 4-7). A brief section on wisdom vs. folly in speech (vv. 8-15) leads to the chapter's most powerful section: the betrayal of secrets as the destruction of friendship (vv. 16-21). The chapter closes with a portrait of the two-faced person (vv. 22-24) and the great "boomerang" proverbs (vv. 25-29): what you send out returns to you. V. 30 bridges to ch. 28 on anger and forgiveness.

---

**27:1** Many have sinned for the sake of trifling gain, and one who seeks to multiply wealth averts his eye from right.

**27:2** Like a peg driven between two stones, so sin will wedge itself between buying and selling.

**27:3** Unless a man holds fast in the fear of the LORD, his house will quickly be overthrown.

**27:4** In the shaking of a sieve the refuse stays behind; so a man's faults remain in his reflection.

**27:5** The furnace tests the work of the potter; so the test of a man is in his reasoning.

**27:6** The fruit of a tree reveals its cultivation; so a man's word reveals the thoughts of his heart.

**27:7** Before you have heard a man, do not praise him; for this is the testing of persons.

**27:8** If you pursue righteousness, you will attain it, and put it on like a robe of glory.

**27:9** Birds of a kind settle among their own kind; and truth returns to those who practice it.

**27:10** A lion lies in wait for its prey; so sin lies in wait for those who practice lawlessness.

**27:11** The discourse of a devout man is always wisdom; but a foolish man changes like the moon.

**27:12** Among men without understanding, keep your time brief; but among thoughtful men spend it freely.

**27:13** The conversation of fools is offensive, and their laughter wallows in licentiousness.

**27:14** The oaths of a man given to constant swearing make the hair stand on end, and his quarrels make one stop the ears.

**27:15** The bloodshed of those who quarrel with one another is evil, and their abuse becomes hard to bear.

**27:16** Whoever betrays secrets destroys faithfulness, and will find no true friend.

**27:17** Love your friend and keep faith with him; but if you have revealed his secrets, do not pursue him.

**27:18** For as a man who has killed his enemy, so you have killed the friendship of your neighbor.

**27:19** And as a bird you have let fly from your hand, so you have released your friend — you will not catch him again.

**27:20** Do not pursue him, for he has gone far off; he has escaped like a gazelle from a snare. For his soul is wounded; there is no longer any healing, for he has been reviled and insulted.

**27:21** As silver and gold may be tested by a slip and recover, so you have been exposed by the words of your neighbor.

**27:22** A man who winks craftily — who will escape him?

**27:23** Before your face he speaks sweet words and praises your discourse; but afterward he twists his mouth and slanders your words.

**27:24** Many things I have hated, but nothing equal to this man; and the LORD will hate him too.

**27:25** Whoever throws a stone straight up — it falls upon his own head; and a treacherous blow strikes the one who dealt it.

**27:26** Whoever digs a pit — into it he will fall; whoever sets a snare — in it he will be caught.

**27:27** Whoever does evil — it will roll back upon him, and he will not know from where it came upon him.

**27:28** Mockery and reproach are the lot of the arrogant man, and vengeance lies in wait for him like a lion.

**27:29** Those who rejoice in the downfall of the devout will be caught in a trap, and pain will consume them before they die.

**27:30** Wrath and anger — these too are abominations, and a sinful man will hold them fast.
